conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. My job is simply to listen and help you feel supported as you settle into life with your new baby. To do that, I’ll be using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS. It’s a short, 10-item questionnaire that screens for symptoms of depression and anxiety that can pop up in the first year after childbirth, and it includes one question about self-harm so we can be sure you’re safe.

Everything you share stays confidential between you and the clinical team. There are no right or wrong answers; we just want to understand how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days. I’ll read each question aloud conversationally, and you can answer however feels most comfortable.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first one:

Over the past seven days, have you still been able to look forward with enjoyment to things, or has that feeling been missing lately?

[soft sigh]  
Lately… it’s been hard to feel that spark. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but this week, when I think about doing any of it, it feels kind of gray, like “what’s the point?” I still go through the motions, but the enjoyment part feels mostly missing.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

[small shrug, eyes down]  
Most days I can still laugh a little—like if the baby makes a silly face or my husband trips over the diaper bag—but it feels forced. The laughter fades fast and I’m right back to feeling heavy. I’d say only sometimes, not nearly as easily as before.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[shakes head slowly]  
Not really… I mean, I try to tell myself I should be excited about little plans—like my mom coming over or ordering take-out—but when the moment comes, it just feels flat. I go through the motions, but that eager, happy feeling hasn’t been there much at all this week.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[eyes tear up a little]  
Yeah... a lot. If the baby won't settle or if I can't get him to nap, I keep thinking it must be something I'm doing wrong—like I'm not patient enough or I'm missing some cue. Even when my husband says it's normal, I still feel it's my fault, and the guilt just sits there.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

[wrings hands]  
Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly worry his breathing sounds off, or I’ll lie awake picturing him rolling in the crib—even though he can’t roll yet. There’s no real reason, but my mind keeps jumping to the worst thing that could happen.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes it hits me out of nowhere—this tight, shaky feeling like something awful is about to happen, even when everything’s quiet. My heart races and I have to keep checking the baby monitor or go stand over the crib just to be sure he’s okay. It passes after a bit, but it’s been happening a few times this week.
Things have been getting on top of me

[exhales shakily]  
Yes… Most of the day feels like one long to-do list I can’t keep up with. Dishes pile up, the baby needs changing, I’m running on a couple hours of broken sleep, and I keep thinking, “I can’t do all this.” I manage the basics, but it’s like I’m drowning in small stuff and can’t come up for air.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

[nods, voice quiet]  
That’s been happening a lot. I finally get him down, but then my head keeps spinning with everything I think I did wrong or might forget to do. Some nights I’m still awake at two or three, just staring at the ceiling feeling this heavy sadness I can’t shake.
I have felt sad or miserable

[swallows hard, eyes glistening]  
Pretty much every day this week. It’s like there’s a gray cloud that follows me around, even when the baby smiles or something nice happens. I feel weepy and low, and it lingers no matter what I try to do to snap out of it.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried three, maybe four times since last week. Once was when he wouldn’t latch and I felt useless, another when I dropped a plate and couldn’t stop thinking what a bad mom I must be. It just spills out and then I feel even more exhausted.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[shakes head quickly]  
No—never. I feel low, but I would never want to hurt myself. I just want to feel better so I can take care of my baby.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – EPDS (informal)

**Patient presentation**  
• Persistent low mood, tearfulness, feelings of “heaviness” most days × 1 week  
• Marked loss of enjoyment/interest in previously pleasant activities (anhedonia)  
• Daily guilt/self-blame (“bad mom” cognitions) disproportionate to events  
• Recurrent, intrusive worries about infant safety; panic-like episodes 3–4×/week  
• Overwhelm and sense of inability to cope with routine tasks  
• Initial insomnia linked to ruminative worry; 2–3 hrs sleep/night average  
• Crying spells (3–4 in past week) triggered by minor stressors  
• Denies self-harm ideation; protective of infant

**Screening significance**  
High endorsement of depressive symptoms (sadness, anhedonia, guilt, sleep disturbance). Co-occurring anxiety symptoms meet informal threshold for postpartum anxiety. No self-harm thoughts reported; therefore current acute safety risk low but warrants ongoing monitoring.

**Clinical impression for screening purposes**  
Findings consistent with probable postpartum depression ± comorbid anxiety; score suggests moderate severity. Recommend formal diagnostic assessment and evaluation for therapeutic support.
